observations:
Torah #280 is a short, tightly structured teaching (20 lines) built around three interlocking thematic domains — commerce, Torah, and faith — which correspond exactly to the three packages identified from the bechina subgraph. The Torah's Kabbalistic structure (Asiyah → Yetzirah, Malkhut rising from klipot) maps directly onto these three packages: Package 1 (commerce/עשיה), Package 2 (Torah/יצירה), Package 3 (faith/Malkhut). There is no fourth independent conceptual domain with explicit bechina language.

The most plausible candidate for a new package would be a 'Worlds/Sefirot' structural package around עשיה, יצירה, מלכות דעשיה — but (a) the dataset only captures עשיה and יצירה as bechina nodes within the existing packages (עשיה belongs to commerce, יצירה belongs to Torah), and (b) the Kabbalistic technical language (חבד, עשיה, יצירה, מלכות) functions in this Torah as the structural vocabulary DESCRIBING how the commerce and Torah packages relate — not as an independent thematic domain. These terms are the medium, not the message.

The missing node מלכות דעשיה (= אמונה, see additions file) would, if added, reinforce Package 3 rather than create a new package. It is the Kabbalistic name for faith at the level of action — the same concept as אמונה, not a distinct domain.

Conclusion: The three-package structure (commerce/sparks, Torah/formation, faith/Jerusalem) fully covers the conceptual topology of Torah #280. No additional independent domain with 3+ bechina-connected concepts exists in the source text beyond what is already captured.
